sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal by the claimant under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act is arising out of the award dated 11.10.2023 passed by Member, First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur (MP) in MACC No.69/2016, whereby the Tribunal has dismissed the claim application of Claimant.

1

entities.text: First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (2) Brief facts of the case are that on 05.07.2017, the claimant Shambhulal and his friend went to Gram Panchayat Sitakhedi, Mandsaur and when he returned from Gram Sitakhedi from his motorcycle bearing registration No.MP14MT-4427 and when he reached Sitamau near S.R. Petrol Pump at 8:00 pm suddenly the respondent No.1 driver of Tractor bearing registration No.MP14AC-7164 driven rashly and negligently hit the claimant due to which the claimant and his friend Mangilal who was sitting in the motorcycle fell down from it and received severe injuries on various parts of the body and his motorcycle was also destroyed.
The police registered the case thereafter against the driver of the offending vehicle (Tractor) and after investigtion, chargesheet was also filed against them.

The claimant further pleaded due to severe injuries he admitted to Sitamau Hospital at Mandsaur (MP) and thereafter he was referred to Gitanjali Hospital at Udaipur (Rajasthan) where he was treated for long time and during his treatment he went to Coma.
( 3) Claimant filed claim petition seeking compensation against the respondents and respondents filed their written statements and denied all the averments pleaded in the claim petition.
(4) Tribunal after framing issues and after taking evidence of both the parties dismissed the claim petition filed by the appellant/claimant.
Being aggrieved by such award, claimant filed this appeal on the ground that Motor Vehicle Act is a social welfare legislation and claim application should not be dismissed on technical ground.

He further submits that Tribunal has wrongly dismissed his claim application on the ground that there is a delay in lodging the F.I.R., hence, prays for setting aside the impugned award and seeking compensation.
(5) On the other hand, counsel for the respondents supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.
(6) I have heard counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal with due care.

(7) According to Ex.P/2, FIR was lodged on 10.11.2017 and accident occurred on 05.07.2017.According to FIR Ex.P/2, the police received information from CSC Sitamau and as per Ex.P/10 which is MLC report which was sent by CSC Sitamau to Police Station and it was received by Police Station on06.07.2017 and thereafter Sub-Inspector Khan was directed to inquire into the matter.
According to Ex.P/10, it was found that the claimant has been brought to the hospital due to severe injuries received by him on various parts of the body due to accident.
In Ex.P/10, it was not mentioned that due to which vehicle the accident had occurred but as per Ex.P/2, it is mentioned that the driver of the offending vehicle has caused the accident.
After investigation, the final report was filed against the driver of offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP14AC-7164.
(8) Counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that FIR was promptly lodged.
He submitted that he had properly explained the delay occurred in lodging FIR.
(9) It well settled that lodging of F.I.R. is fatal in deciding motor accident claim case but, lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings.
If claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.

The Apex Court in case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226 in Para 20 and 21 has held as under:-

2 20.

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.

Delay in lodging the FIR thus,
cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered toimplicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.
(10) Counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that claimant was injured in a motor accident case and he was admitted in the hospital for treatment and after treatment, he lodged FIR (Ex.P/2).
(11) Considering the evidence of the claimant, it is found that accident occurred on 05.07.2017 and claimant lodged FIR on 10.11.2017.

He has admitted in his cross-examination that he was discharged from the hospital on 17.07.2017 and it is clear from the discharge ticket Ex.P/30 that claimant/appellant was admitted in hospital from 06.07.2017 and discharged on 17.07.2017.

Thereafter he was in his house but he never went to the Police Station to give information about the incident and for the registration of the offending vehicle and he never tried to given written report to the Police Station regarding the accident.

The claimant had not given proper explanation as to why he did not lodge report after discharge from the hospital and it was the duty of the claimant to explain as to why he did not lodge the FIR during the aforesaid period.
(12) It is true that Motor Vehicles Act is a social welfare legislation but it does not mean that a person will misuse it.
It is also true that delay in lodging FIR is not fatal to the case, if claimant gives satisfactory explanation in respect of delay in lodging the FIR.

But, perusal of the evidence of the claim, it is found that claimant is unable to explain the delay in lodging the FIR So in the considered opinion of this Court, as claimant is unable to explain the delay in lodging FIR, the Tribunal has rightly disbelieved the evidence of the claimant and rightly found that claimant is unable to prove Shambhulal vs Mukesh on 9 May, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192946944/
3 that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently due to which claimant received injuries.

(13) In view of the aforesaid discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, the trial court has rightly rejected the claim application of the appellant/claimant, hence, no case for interference is made out with the order passed by the trial court.
Accordingly, the present appeal is dismissed.
